papers.title_in_file: Quantum-Assisted Solution Paths for the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, TSP results (QAOA, VQE, optimizer and penalty sections), discussion and outlook; appendix tables skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study of QAOA and VQE on small TSP instances derived from a capacitated vehicle routing problem, with a proposed QUBO formulation and a feasibility-based performance metric.

assertions.value: The authors report that QAOA results on their TSP instances are generally of limited quality because the algorithm does not reach the energy threshold for feasible TSP solutions, while the VQE reaches the energy threshold and shows a better performance.
quotes: Results of QAOA are generally of limited quality because the algorithm
does not reach the energy threshold for feasible TSP solutions,
the VQE reaches the energy threshold and shows a better performance.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one simulation study on toy instances.
assertions.reader_inference: Result is for toy TSP instances with an out-of-the-box QAOA; it does not show QAOA cannot work on routing problems in general.

assertions.value: The authors state that the algorithms are tested on TSP instances with 4, 5 and 6 nodes, and that on the 27-qubit IBM system only the 4-node TSP could be solved satisfactorily on real hardware.
assertions.anchor: Section IV (results), Table II discussion, p.7-8
quotes: The algorithms are tested on instances with 4, 5 and 6 nodes derived from the blue part in the CVRP
the best optimizers (Powell and NFT) on the 27-qubit IBM system in Ehningen.
Only the 4-node TSP could be solved satisfactorily on real hardware.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup and scope.
assertions.reader_inference: The tested problems are toy sizes far below the industry-sized problems the paper itself describes.

assertions.value: The authors report that at an Ising approximation ratio around 97 - 98% the feasibility rises significantly and is close to zero below, and they state the high ratio required is partly caused by the problem formulation and might be avoided with a different encoding.
quotes: at an (Ising) approximation ratio around 97 - 98%, the feasibility rises significantly and is close to zero below.
The high approximation ratio required is partly caused by the problem formulation and might be avoided with a different encoding.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical observation from one study; the encoding explanation is the authors' conjecture.

assertions.value: The paper proves an exact mapping from randomly initialized circuits to a set of Clifford circuits and reports an efficient classical method to compute the gradient of the cost function and its variance for a wide class of variational quantum circuits.

variance for a wide class of variational
quantum circuits. Our scheme relies on our proof of an exact mapping from randomly initialized
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states it proves the mapping and the efficiency.

papers.title_in_file: Photovoltaic power forecasting using quantum machine learning
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, methods overview, results and discussion, conclusion; circuit-analysis section skimmed
papers.what_it_is: An empirical study of hybrid quantum-classical neural networks (HQNN, HQLSTM, HQSeq2Seq) for photovoltaic power time-series forecasting, run on a classical state-vector simulator; authors are at Terra Quantum.

assertions.value: The authors report that the HQLSTM with only 1109 parameters achieved a test MAE of 0.0343 and a test MSE of 0.0058, while the LSTM with 2857 parameters had scores of 0.0570 and 0.0096.

assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study on one public dataset, simulated.

papers.title_in_file: Assessing the Benefits and Risks of Quantum Computers
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, contents, conclusion and discussion, and the cryptanalysis risk passages; the long literature-survey sections 2 to 5 were not read in full
papers.what_it_is: A long review by authors from IBM, NIST and others of the potential benefits of quantum computing and its risk to public-key cryptography, with recommendations.

assertions.value: The authors state that the maturity of currently available quantum computers is not yet at a level such that they can be used in production for large-scale, industrially-relevant problems, and that they are not believed to currently pose security risks.
quotes: The maturity of currently-available quantum computers is not yet at a level such that they can be used in production for large-scale, industrially-relevant problems, and they are not believed to currently pose security risks.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author assessment drawn from a literature review; the first author is at IBM, a quantum hardware vendor.

assertions.value: The authors conclude there is a credible expectation that quantum computers will be capable of performing computations which are economically-impactful before they will be capable of performing ones which are cryptographically-relevant.
quotes: we conclude there is a credible expectation that quantum computers will be capable of performing computations which are economically-impactful before they will be capable of performing ones which are cryptographically-relevant.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author judgment, not a measured result; authors include employees of quantum vendors.
assertions.reader_inference: A forecast of the ordering of two milestones, not a date.

assertions.value: The authors state that, from their analysis of current and known algorithms for cryptanalysis, the required circuits exceed in size those that can be run by current and near-future quantum computers.
quotes: we find they require circuits of a size exceeding those that can be run by current and near-future quantum computers
assertions.certainty_reason: An author analysis built on published resource estimates; the authors acknowledge algorithmic improvements may change it.

assertions.value: The paper cites an analysis suggesting RSA-2048 is unlikely to be factored (< 5% confidence) before 2039, based on a statistical model extrapolating current quantum computing hardware progress.
quotes: One suggests RSA-2048 is unlikely to be factored (< 5% confidence) before 2039, based on a statistical model extrapolating current quantum computing hardware progress
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the paper attributes to other work.

papers.version_note: The record id suggests a quantum paper, but the file is a classical machine learning paper on weight quantization of GANs (low-bit number formats). It contains no quantum computing.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, case study on existing quantization methods, results tables and conclusion
papers.what_it_is: A classical machine learning paper that quantizes the weights of generative adversarial networks to a few bits using an EM-based method.

assertions.value: The authors report that experiments on CIFAR10 and CelebA show their QGAN method can quantize GANs to even 1-bit or 2-bit representations with results of quality comparable to original models.
quotes: Experiments on CIFAR10 and CelebA show that QGAN can quantize GANs to even 1-bit or 2-bit representations with results of quality comparable to original models.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study using Inception Score.
assertions.reader_inference: Name collision: this QGAN is classical weight quantization, not a quantum GAN.

assertions.value: The authors report that the existing quantization methods they tried do not generate samples with reasonable quality on GANs, which they attribute to underrepresentation of quantized values in model weights.
quotes: none of them generates samples with reasonable quality because of the underrepresentation of quantized values in model weights
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical observation from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the discriminator is more sensitive than the generator to the number of quantized bits.
quotes: the discriminator is more sensitive than the generator to the number of quantized bits
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical observation on DCGAN and related models.

papers.title_in_file: A Survey on Quantum Machine Learning: Basics, Current Trends, Challenges, Opportunities, and the Road Ahead
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, barren-plateau and challenges passages, and the conclusion; the algorithm, hardware and software sections were not read in full
papers.what_it_is: A survey of quantum machine learning covering algorithms, datasets, hardware, software, applications and open challenges.

assertions.value: The authors state that QML faces significant challenges related to size and noise constraints, which affect the scalability and reliability of these systems.
quotes: QML faces significant challenges related to the size and noise constraints, which affect the scalability and reliability of these systems.
assertions.certainty_reason: A survey authors' summary judgment.

assertions.value: The authors state that QML algorithms are still in their early stages and may not yet match the accuracy of mature classical ML algorithms.
quotes: Although QML algorithms are still in their early stages and may not yet match the accuracy of mature classical ML algorithms
assertions.certainty_reason: A survey authors' summary judgment, not a measured comparison.

assertions.value: The survey states that the barren plateau phenomenon, where gradients vanish exponentially with system size, significantly hinders the training of deeper or wider QML models.
quotes: The barren plateau phenomenon, where gradients vanish exponentially with system size, significantly hinders the training of deeper or wider QML models
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the survey attributes to prior work.

papers.title_in_file: Speeding up quantum perceptron via shortcuts to adiabaticity
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results on the quantum perceptron and the discussion of the minimum-time comparison; methods and supplementary parts not read in full
papers.what_it_is: A theory and simulation paper designing a faster quantum perceptron sigmoid response through invariant-based inverse engineering of a control field.

assertions.value: The authors propose a quantum perceptron in which a control field is inversely engineered, giving a rapid nonlinear response with a sigmoid activation function, and report faster overall performance than quasi-adiabatic protocols and enhanced robustness against imperfections in the controls.
quotes: we propose a speed-up quantum perceptron where a control field on the perceptron is inversely engineered
This results in faster overall perceptron performance compared to quasi-adiabatic protocols,
as well as in enhanced robustness against imperfections in the controls.
assertions.certainty_reason: A numerical result from one study; no experiment is reported in the parts read.

assertions.value: The authors report that for N = 3 the smallest t_f such that C < 0.01 is satisfied is 0.2 for their inverse-engineering method, while employing techniques based on FAQUAD this is at t_f = 0.3.

based on FAQUAD, this is at t f = 0.3.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Generative Adversarial Networks For Anomaly Detection In High Energy Physics
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results (simulation and hardware), effective dimension section, discussion and conclusions; theory and algorithm sections skimmed
papers.what_it_is: An empirical study of a quantum GAN-based anomaly detector for particle-physics events, run in simulation and on an IBM Quantum processor; authors are at IBM Quantum and CERN.

assertions.value: The authors report that the quantum models were trained with 10 times fewer data samples than the classical models but still achieve comparable accuracy, AUC, precision and F1 scores.
quotes: It is worth stressing that the quantum models were trained with 10 times fewer data samples than the classical models, but still achieve comparable accuracy, AUC, precision and F1 scores.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from simulation on an artificial dataset, one study.
assertions.reader_inference: Results come from noiseless and noisy simulation; the paper also states the classical model slightly outperforms the quantum one for fewer than seven features.

assertions.value: The authors report that on the IBM Quantum processor ibmq belem, for the Graviton task, the A-qGAN AUC curve is lower than for the classical and noiseless methods, and the figure legend gives AUC 0.84 classical, 0.81 simulation and 0.74 hardware.
assertions.anchor: Section IV B and the ROC figure legend, p.8
quotes: Compared to the classical and noiseless methods, the AUC curve of the A-qGAN evaluated on the quantum hardware is lower.
Classical (AUC: 0.84) Simulation (AUC: 0.81) Hardware (AUC: 0.74)
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one hardware run set; training used reduced epochs and data.
assertions.reader_inference: The hardware result is below both the classical and the noiseless simulated result.

assertions.value: The authors state that a lack of data is typically not a problem in this type of HEP task, and that the amount of training data will even increase in the next years.
quotes: It should, however, be mentioned that a lack of data is typically not a problem in this type of HEP task.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of the limit on the value of its result.
assertions.reader_inference: This weakens the practical relevance of the 10-times-fewer-samples result for HEP, which the authors suggest may matter in other data-scarce fields.

assertions.value: The authors report that the effective dimension of the quantum model is always larger than that of the classical model, which they say indicates a higher expressibility.
quotes: The effective dimension of the quantum model is always larger than for the classical model which indicates a higher expressibility.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study; models have a similar number of trainable parameters.
